notes: Four-workload enriched dataset. IDS and SUNCATCHER from Thummala & Falco (2025) extended to 30 variables. JWST and RST estimated from published mission specs: JWST Pocket Guide (STScI 2023), Roman Science Requirements Document (SRD-0001 2024), GSFC instrument specs, DSN scheduling data. Latency for telescope workloads expressed in seconds (not ms) — see per-workload notes. All values are best-estimates for research purposes; RST values will be updated with professor consultation.

IDS.description: Spacecraft intrusion detection system for CDHS. Mission-critical, 5-year design life, hard real-time 250ms latency requirement. From Thummala & Falco (2025), extended to 30 variables.

Offload ratio.description: Fraction of task routable to this tier [0,1]

Data sensitivity.description: Classification level of data processed (0=open..4=SCI); lower is lower risk

FC_mem_type.description: [FC Stage 1] Memory SEU robustness score: SRAM=0.3,NOR=0.5,MRAM=1.0

SUNCATCHER.description: Large-scale neural network training. Google Suncatcher concept (arXiv 2511.19468). 10-year mission life. Tiers: LEO TPU constellation, ground TPU DC, ground GPU DC, hybrid split.

JWST.description: James Webb Space Telescope science data calibration pipeline (NIRCam/NIRSpec/MIRI Stage 1-3). Workload: from raw detector readouts to science-grade calibrated exposures. JWST orbits Sun-Earth L2 at 1.5M km. Latency in HOURS (multiply ms column by 3600000 to convert). Design life 10 years (launched Dec 2021). Sources: STScI JWST Pocket Guide 2023, JDox calibration pipeline docs, DSN scheduling data.

Latency (hrs).description: Time from observation completion to calibrated science product

Science quality (0-1).description: 1.0=fully calibrated pipeline product; 0.65=basic compression+CR flagging only

Contact duty cycle.description: Fraction of time data can be transferred

TX power (W).description: Satellite transmitter power for this tier

Rad dose margin (krad).description: L2 environment ~2 krad/yr; RAD750 rated 1 Mrad

Autonomy compat.description: Fraction of pipeline executable without ground commanding

FC_ICDH._notes: BAE Systems RAD750 processor at 200MHz, 256MB SDRAM. Performs lossless compression (ICER), cosmic ray flagging, guide star acquisition. No full calibration pipeline possible onboard. L2 radiation: ~2 krad/yr x 10yr = 20 krad; RAD750 rated 1 Mrad -> margin 980 krad.

GSE_STSCI._notes: STScI Baltimore science operations center + DSN receive nodes (Madrid, Goldstone, Canberra). JWST has 2 contact windows/day ~1hr each via DSN Ka-band at 28 Mbps. Stage 1 calibration (detector-level corrections) completed at STScI edge within 6 hours of data receipt.
GSE_STSCI.Contact duty cycle_note: STScI nominal: ~10 hr/day total contact across 2 daily contacts (0.42); downlink-only conservative is ~0.33. Original value 0.08 reflected a non-nominal commissioning scenario. Sources: STScI JWST User Documentation (JWST Data Volume / SSR page); NASA Science Blog.

TDC_MAST._notes: STScI MAST archive + full calibration pipeline (Stages 1-2-3). Full science-grade products including flux calibration, WCS, source extraction. Available to PI within 24-48hrs. Also accessible via Barbara A. Mikulski Archive.

RST.description: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Wide Field Survey data reduction pipeline. Roman WFI: 18 H4RG-10 detectors, 300 megapixel, 0.281 sq-deg FOV. Target: ~500 GB/day downlink. Planned launch 2027, 6-year prime mission at Sun-Earth L2. Tiers: FC (onboard processor), GSE (ground station edge), TDC (IPAC/STScI science center). Values estimated from Roman SRD-0001 (2024), IPAC Roman Science Support Center docs, and extrapolation from JWST heritage. PLACEHOLDER: update with professor consultation.

FC_ROMAN._notes: Roman onboard processor: estimated ~2 GFLOPS (upgraded vs JWST RAD750, likely rad-hard RISC-V or PowerPC derivative). 64 GB solid-state recorder. L2 radiation 2 krad/yr x 6yr = 12 krad; rad-hard processor rated ~200 krad -> margin 188 krad. Onboard tasks: lossless compression 2:1, persistence correction, cosmic ray flagging, guide window processing for fine guidance sensor.

GSE_GODDARD._notes: NASA GSFC White Sands Complex + Goddard Space Flight Center science operations. Roman downlinks via Ka-band at 500 Mbps (vs JWST 28 Mbps — major upgrade). Contact: 2x ~2hr windows/day at White Sands. GSE performs quick-look reduction (Level 1 products) for survey scheduling decisions within same operational day.
GSE_GODDARD.Contact duty cycle_note: Updated from 0.17 (single-DSN baseline) to 0.45 (Roman uses NEN/DSN/ESA/JAXA combined, ~10-12 hr/day). Matches the 0.45 used for ROMAN_TRANSIENT GSE. Original 0.17 was the single-DSN 4-hr/day worst case. Source: Roman SRD, NASA/GSFC; matches STScI nominal for JWST (0.42).

TDC_IPAC._notes: IPAC at Caltech (Roman Science Support Center) + STScI archive (Barbara A. Mikulski Archive). Full Level 2/3 pipeline: flat field, flux calibration, WCS solution, co-addition, source catalogs. Estimated 12-24hr turnaround for survey data. ~10 PB/yr archive scale. Cost estimate: $0.50/obs at cloud-scale compute.

ROMAN_TRANSIENT.description: Roman Space Telescope transient detection and follow-up pipeline (real-time, layered on continuous WFI survey). Regular alerting profile (24 hr latency budget for broker dissemination).
ROMAN_TRANSIENT.odc_motivation: Quantifies value-of-L2-companion-ODC under three variants: A=TRL3 concept (default; will be TRL-gated for mission-critical), B=TRL7 mature (override at runtime), C=ODC-ablation (3-tier).

ODC TRL=3 baseline (Variant A); Variant B overrides to TRL=7; Variant C ablates ODC entirely. Motivating programs: Project Suncatcher, Starcloud, ESA CDF orbital data centre study.

v5: JWST GSE_STSCI Contact duty cycle corrected 0.08 -> 0.42 (STScI nominal). Original value reflected commissioning, not operations. Affects JWST nonlinear results: contact-saturation knee moves from p_GSE > 0.08 to p_GSE > 0.42.

v6: RST GSE_GODDARD Contact duty cycle corrected 0.17 -> 0.45 (multi-station NEN/DSN/ESA/JAXA aggregate). Same correction class as JWST v5. Affects RST nonlinear contact-saturation knee and feasibility rate; expected to improve RST linear-vs-NL validity ratio significantly.

notes_appended.source: Measured on the cfs_ids_workload NASA cFS application running on a NASA TRL-8 spaceflight computer. The application implements a generic spacecraft intrusion-detection workload (CCSDS-style header validation, rolling source-rate anomaly check, CRC-32 payload verification, with a NORMAL -> SUSPECT -> BLOCKED state machine using K-clean recovery) and carries no sensor-specific semantics. Per-task CLOCK_MONOTONIC instrumentation around the IDS pipe-receive and processing path, driven by a Poisson injector (apps/ids_loadgen) at controlled lambda. Calibration at lambda=5/s (rho ~ 0.02) yields E[T_svc] = 4.00 ms and p99 = 5.62 ms; jitter (p99 - median) ~ 1.6 ms, rounded to 2. Throughput (GFLOPS) is not measured by this experiment and is taken from vendor specifications.
